newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium slumps, dented by LME and dollar.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium slumps, dented by LME and dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures slumped across the board on Wednesday, hit by the metal's decline on the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight and the dollar's retreat against the yen, traders said.

Yet traders were divided over the direction, with some worried over the absence of bargain-hunters, while the others remained confident as aluminium showed resilience against copper's steep fall on the LME overnight.
One trader said: "I'm worried. The (TOCOM) futures renewed their contract lows but we saw stop-loss selling instead of bargain-hunters."
Another trader said she was watching whether the benchmark three month aluminium on the LME would hold the next support at the $1,550 per tonne.
Benchmark April 1998 lost 3.9 yen to end at 186.1 yen per kg, while others fell between 2.7 yen and 4.0 yen.
The dollar dived against the yen in Tokyo on Wednesday, sent staggering by a strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey.
In London overnight, three month aluminium slipped $13 to $1,577 per tonne, while flagship copper gave up $74 to $2,437 on hints the worst of the supply tightness might have passed.
